test_title: PYST 44 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The crowd had __gathered at__ the streets to witness the parade.
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. gathered on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition "on" is commonly used with "streets" to indicate the physical location or place where people are gathered.
 
• In the context of the sentence, "gathered on the streets" is grammatically correct because it refers to people being present on the surface of the streets to witness the parade.
 
• The other options ("gathered into," "gathered aside") are incorrect because they do not fit the context of the sentence. "No substitution" is also incorrect as the sentence requires improvement.

---

Correct sentence: *The crowd had gathered on the streets to witness the parade.*

---

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**

 
 
• **"On":** Indicates a surface or place where an event occurs (e.g., "on the streets," "on the table").
 
• **"Into":** Suggests movement or direction inside something (e.g., "into the building").
 
• **"Aside":** Implies movement to the side or away (e.g., "step aside").
 
 
 
• In this sentence, "on" is the most appropriate preposition to describe the physical location of the crowd.
